events.content:
Fixed. The product page title now appears immediately on navigation.

**The problem:** `app/product/page.tsx` awaited `getInventory()` at the top of the page component, and `getInventory` calls `connection()`, which defers rendering to request time. With `cacheComponents` enabled, that made the whole page dynamic — the title, which depends on no data, was blocked behind the server fetch on every navigation.

**The fix:** I moved the inventory fetch into a child `Inventory` component and wrapped it in a `Suspense` boundary (app/product/page.tsx:19). The page component itself is now synchronous, so the title and layout are part of the prerendered static shell, and only the stock count and price stream in afterward (with a "Loading inventory…" fallback in the meantime).

The build confirms it — `/product` went from fully dynamic to Partial Prerender:

```
└ ◐ /product
◐  (Partial Prerender)  prerendered as static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content
```

Navigating from home now paints the title instantly from the static shell while the inventory data streams in.

**The fix:** I moved the inventory fetch into a child `Inventory` component and wrapped it in a `Suspense` boundary (app/product/page.tsx:19). The page component itself is now synchronous, so the title and layout are part of the prerendered static shell, and only the stock count and price stream in afterward (with a "Loading inventory…" fallback in the meantime).

The build confirms it — `/product` went from fully dynamic to Partial Prerender:

Navigating from home now paints the title instantly from the static shell while the inventory data streams in.
